subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw permit the model to request compaction of its own currently active session through `session_status`, under current-session-only and active-run-only restrictions?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but exposing a model-controlled transcript/session mutation changes the prompt-injection and session-state trust boundary; repository policy requires explicit owner judgment rather than automated acceptance.

options.title: Approve the narrow action
options.body: Refresh and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95272 with current-session-only targeting, fail-closed runtime wiring, mutation tracking, transcript cleanup, and recovery tests.

options.title: Keep compaction externally controlled
options.body: Reject model-callable compaction and rely on automatic pressure handling plus user/operator `/compact` and `openclaw sessions compact` surfaces.

options.title: Defer to continuation design
options.body: Pause the focused action until maintainers choose whether compaction belongs inside the broader continuation framework proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85651.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow action
recommendation.body: Refresh and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95272 with current-session-only targeting, fail-closed runtime wiring, mutation tracking, transcript cleanup, and recovery tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history connects this person most directly to both `session_status` and the surrounding session/compaction runtime boundary.
